doc.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Jaco, honors, teaching and looking ahead
title: Listening to younger players
summary: He praises younger musicians, among them Terri Lyne Carrington, Vijay Iyer and Rudresh Mahanthappa.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: So, that’s it. That’s what I… I’m into now. I’m always being into. Even… but now, I try to say this as much with fewer notes. Is it Miles who said, “Less is more”? Something like that. And okay, just listen. Keep listen. Keep listening. I listen to… for instance, this lady, Terri Lyne Carrington. Isn’t she [mean?] [inaudible]. I think she’s mean, you know.

And I think these days, she’s companion… she has a companion, Greg Osby. They’re together. This… that’s a little… Greg Osby or Steve Coleman. The sound remains… their touch and their tone production is, without a doubt is from your side of the street. [laughs] But somehow the blue note… you know, I’m old-fashioned. I mean that… [plays harmonica] Well, I’m exaggerating now, you know. And [inaudible]… [plays] You know? But day to day, they can do that. But they… somehow their runs I don’t always… but more power to them, you know. Who am I, you know?
Are there any youngsters that catch your ear? Anybody playing from the younger generation that you..
I listen to them, and there’s a few trumpet players. [Patch?] something. And a guitar player. I have him there. [inaudible] And this Indian fellow… Eli [Jai?]…
Oh. Vijay Iyer. He’s a piano player. And then Rudresh Mahanthappa.
Yeah. And oh. The tenor playing with him, I like. Rudish…
And he sounds like… he’s a singer, a religious singer of this country. [imitates] I beg your pardon. But he sounds… that’s it. I have it here and everything. I listen to those cats.

And here and there, something’s [inaudible]. I’m not, I’m not, I would say, this… I’m still [rubbable?]. [laughs] I’m still a, you know, it’s not [that I’m just standstill?]. There’s still a little balls here and there for some of that shit. [laughs]
[laughs] That’s great. Keep an open mind, right?
